summary: This article explains how cameras capture light to make a picture, basic ideas like framing and lighting, how photography changed from film to digital, and how photography works as both documentation and art.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Photography: Capturing a Moment” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: the amount of light that reaches the camera to make a picture
the part of a camera that opens and closes to let light in
using an electronic sensor and computer parts instead of film

challengeTerms.def: the size of a camera's opening that controls how much light enters and how much of the scene stays in focus
the electronic part inside a digital camera that turns light into a picture
to record something exactly as it happened, as proof or a record

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a photograph can tell a true story all by itself, without any words? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how exposure and composition each affect the final look of a photograph.
struggling: Pre-teach exposure, shutter, and digital with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses aperture, sensor, and document to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
